name: Amazon S3
oneLiner: Storage is the boring part - the requests and the egress are what actually blow up your bill.
trap: PUT/COPY/POST/LIST cost about 10x more per request than GET, and DELETEs are free. IA and Glacier classes add retrieval fees, a 128 KB minimum object size, and early-delete charges.

name: Amazon S3 Glacier
oneLiner: Cheap to park data, expensive to want it back - retrieval bills per GB and per restore request.
trap: A restore costs a per-request fee AND a per-GB retrieval fee, and Expedited/Standard/Bulk changes both. Delete before 90 days (Deep Archive: 180) and you still pay the remaining days.

name: Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS)
oneLiner: You pay for the size you provisioned, not what you used, and snapshots keep billing after the volume is gone.
trap: Detached volumes still bill in full. gp3 IOPS and throughput above baseline bill separately, EBS direct API blocks bill per request, and archived snapshots have a 90-day minimum.

name: Amazon Elastic File System (EFS)
oneLiner: Storage is only half of it - with Elastic throughput every GB you read or write gets metered too.
trap: Elastic throughput bills per GB read AND written, direction-agnostic. IA and Archive add data-access fees on every read, a 128 KiB minimum file size, and Archive has a 90-day minimum.

name: Amazon FSx
oneLiner: Four different file systems under one name, each billing provisioned capacity plus provisioned throughput.
trap: Throughput capacity and SSD IOPS are provisioned and billed separately from storage. Once ONTAP capacity-pool or Lustre Intelligent-Tiering holds your data, every read and write adds a request charge.

name: AWS Backup
oneLiner: Backups bill per GB-month like storage, but restoring costs extra and cold storage locks you in.
trap: Restores are charged per GB, so the stored backup is not the whole bill. Cold-tier backups have a 90-day minimum, so deleting early still pays out the remaining days.

name: AWS Storage Gateway
oneLiner: The rare AWS service that charges you to write data IN and nothing to read it back out.
trap: Inverted from everything else: you pay per GB written to AWS (capped per gateway per month) and reads are free. The S3 or EBS behind it bills separately.

name: AWS DataSync
oneLiner: A flat per-GB toll on everything you move, either direction, on top of what S3 and EFS charge you.
trap: The per-GB fee is direction-agnostic and is only DataSync's cut. S3 LIST/HEAD/GET/PUT requests and cross-region transfer bill on top. Enhanced mode adds a per-task-execution fee.

name: Amazon S3 Express One Zone
oneLiner: Built for request-heavy work: requests are dirt cheap, storage is not, and bytes moved are metered.
trap: Unlike S3 Standard it also bills per GB uploaded and retrieved on top of the per-request fee. Storage costs multiples of S3 Standard, so it punishes idle data.

name: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery
oneLiner: One flat hourly fee per source server - the real cost is the EBS and EC2 it quietly runs for you.
trap: The per-server hour is the small part. A staging EBS volume per source disk, snapshots and replication EC2 instances bill under EBS/EC2 and run 24/7 even when you never fail over.

name: Amazon File Cache
oneLiner: Bills like a provisioned file system - you buy cache capacity by the GB-month, warm or not.
trap: Throughput is not its own line item; it is bundled into capacity, so you buy GB to get MB/s. Cross-AZ and VPC-peering traffic is charged per GB in BOTH directions.

name: AWS Snow Family
oneLiner: You rent a physical box by the day; importing into S3 is free, exporting out of it is not.
trap: Data transfer INTO AWS is free, but export jobs pay normal S3 data-transfer-out per GB. The job fee covers a fixed window of on-site days; sitting on the device past that bills per extra day.
